title: FREE_FIRST_DATA
universal_lens: Free-first data architecture enforces a binary cost structure: zero-cost for cleared facts, justified cost for odds. This maps to a constrained optimization problem where \mathcal{L}(\text{data}) = \sum_{i} \mathbb{1}_{\text{free}_i} \cdot c_i + \mathbb{1}_{\text{paid}_i} \cdot p_i, \text{subject to } \forall i, \text{quality} \geq \theta.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian belief updating over verified free data streams, using conformal prediction to maintain calibrated uncertainty bounds. The system computes posterior probabilities over event outcomes using \mathcal{P}(E|D_{\text{free}}) \propto \mathcal{P}(D_{\text{free}}|E) \cdot \mathcal{P}(E), where \mathcal{P}(E) is prior and \mathcal{P}(D_{\text{free}}|E) is likelihood from cleared sources.
gse_mapping: GSE applies dynamic state transitions governed by a Markov decision process over sport-specific ingestion policies. Each transition \tau_{t \to t+1} = \mathcal{T}(s_t, a_t) is conditioned on \mathcal{S}_{\text{free}}(t) \cup \mathcal{S}_{\text{paid}}(t), with reward function \mathcal{R}(s_t, a_t) = \mathbb{1}_{\text{coverage}} \cdot \mathcal{Q}(s_t) - \lambda \cdot \mathcal{C}(a_t).

primitives.name: Free-First Data Wiring
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Free-First Data Architecture **Goal:** run the stats platform on $0 of paid data wherever a free, cleared source covers the need — without lowering quality.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{L}(\\text{data})': 'Total data cost in USD', '\\mathbb{1}_{\\text{free}_i}': 'Indicator variable for free data source', '\\mathbb{1}_{\\text{paid}_i}': 'Indicator variable for paid data source', 'c_i': 'Cost of free data source i in USD', 'p_i': 'Cost of paid data source i in USD'}
primitives.assumptions: All free data sources are cleared and verified. Quality of free data matches or exceeds paid alternatives.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When no free source covers a required data type, \mathbb{1}_{\text{free}_i} = 0 and \mathbb{1}_{\text{paid}_i} = 1.

layer2.mapping: The free-first wiring is isomorphic to a constraint optimization problem where the objective function minimizes cost subject to quality constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-source validation metrics and cost tracking logs.

primitives.name: Paid Call Justification
primitives.verbatim_quote: The spend guard (`paidCallJustified`) enforces this per call; in-season gating keeps the Odds API's free credits for sports actually playing.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{J}(\\text{call})': 'Justification score for paid call', '\\mathcal{Q}(\\text{data})': 'Data quality threshold', '\\mathcal{C}(\\text{call})': 'Cost of call in USD', '\\mathbb{1}_{\\text{in-season}}': 'Indicator for in-season sports'}
primitives.assumptions: Only calls with \mathcal{J}(\text{call}) > \theta are allowed. In-season gating prevents waste of free credits.

layer2.mapping: Derived from the free-first wiring kernel, this primitive defines the decision boundary for paid data usage.
layer2.telemetry: Call justification logs and in-season status indicators.

primitives.name: Free Coverage Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: `freeCoverageMatrix()` + `planIngestion()` show exactly what to clear to remove spend.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{M}_{ij}': 'Coverage matrix element indicating if source i covers sport j', '\\mathcal{C}_{ij}': 'Cost of source i for sport j', '\\mathcal{F}(\\text{clear})': 'Function to clear unused paid sources'}
primitives.assumptions: Each sport has at least one free source covering it. Clearing unused paid sources reduces cost.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \mathcal{M}_{ij} = 1 for all j, \mathcal{F}(\text{clear}) removes all paid dependencies.

layer2.mapping: The matrix is derived from the free-first wiring and ingestion planning logic to optimize cost reduction.
layer2.telemetry: Coverage matrix outputs and ingestion plan execution logs.

reasoning_traces.think:
The free-first data architecture is modeled as a constrained optimization problem where the goal is to minimize total data cost while maintaining quality thresholds. The core operator \mathcal{L}(\text{data}) = \sum_{i} \mathbb{1}_{\text{free}_i} \cdot c_i + \mathbb{1}_{\text{paid}_i} \cdot p_i ensures that only necessary paid data is used. The justification mechanism \mathcal{J}(\text{call}) acts as a binary gate, enforcing that paid calls are only made when quality requirements cannot be met by free sources. The coverage matrix \mathcal{M}_{ij} enables systematic identification of redundant paid dependencies. Failure modes include misclassification of data quality, incorrect coverage mappings, or bypassing the spend guard. Dualities arise between free and paid data usage, where each paid call must justify its cost against the potential for free alternatives. The system's robustness depends on the integrity of the clearance process and the accuracy of the quality thresholds.
